subject: Feedback discrepancy: Jordan Lee (Backend Engineer) — leveling + offer
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Feedback discrepancy: Jordan Lee (Backend Engineer)

Team —

I'm escalating a discrepancy on the panel feedback for Jordan Lee (Backend Engineer). I interviewed Jordan last week and believe their technical and system-design work demonstrates readiness for L3. The take-home, whiteboard, and reference notes all point to someone who

- designed for scalability (clear sharding/partitioning plan)
- demonstrated pragmatic tradeoffs under latency/cost constraints
- delivered a strong take-home with clear code and test coverage

However, two panel reviewers recorded a "Not ready for L3" rating citing surface-level concerns about algorithmic depth. I disagree and think this is a leveling disagreement rather than a clear fail. Jordan is also on a tight timeline — TalentScout tells me there's an offer on the table from an external company (will lose candidate if we don't move fast).

Action items I need from HR:
- Quick calibration to align on rubric interpretation and confirm leveling (L2 vs L3).
- If HR concurs with L3, permission to extend an offer in the range $150–165k base + equity band A (pref 4/5).
- If not, guidance on what we can offer to keep the candidate engaged and how to document the calibration.

Attached: Jordan_Lee_interview_notes.pdf, panel_feedback.xlsx

I appreciate a quick turnaround — if we can resolve before EOD Thursday we stand a strong chance to close.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Engineering Manager, Core Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feedback discrepancy: Jordan Lee (Backend Engineer)

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for flagging this and for the detailed summary. I can take this on and run a quick calibration. To help expedite: can you send a 1-paragraph summary (2–3 bullets) of the key evidence that supports L3 (impact examples, complexity handled, edge cases covered)? Also confirm the exact target comp band you want us to consider and whether there are any hiring committee constraints.

Plan:
- I'll review the attached notes and panel feedback.
- If needed, schedule a 30-min calibration call tomorrow morning (I've tentatively penciled a slot at 10:00am PT) and invite Vivek for final sign-off on leveling and comp stretch.
- I'll prepare a brief memo capturing the calibration decision for the candidate file + Greenhouse.

If this is urgent for closing, Priya, can you share the candidate's competing offer details so we can model counter scenarios?

Laura Bennett
Senior HR Business Partner
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feedback discrepancy: Jordan Lee (Backend Engineer)

Hannah / Laura —

Quick note from my interview / writeup (attached as dev_notes.txt). I want to be explicit about why I flagged this as leaning L2:
- System design answer was solid on reliability but lacked depth on read/write scaling strategies for multi-region failover (no clear consensus on leader election or cross-region replication latency tradeoffs).
- Coding problem: correct but the optimal complexity solution using amortized data structures was not proposed; candidate implemented simpler approach which may not be sufficient for our highest-throughput paths.
- Probing on past production incidents didn't surface strong ownership examples for cross-service migrations.

I'm open to calibration — my vote was conservative given the candidate will work on critical infra. If the team wants to stretch to L3, I want to ensure we document concrete expectations and identify 90-day success criteria.

— Dev

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feedback discrepancy: Jordan Lee (Backend Engineer)

Thanks Dev — appreciate the specifics. A couple quick clarifications that I think change the weighting here:

- Take-home assignment showed the candidate intentionally chose a different approach to improve consistency under write-heavy load; they explicitly called out leader-election tradeoffs and proposed a light-weight raft-based approach for critical partitions. That was in the repo and tests.
- On the coding task, the candidate provided a follow-up note during debrief explaining why they preferred a simpler approach for maintainability; they proposed optimization steps (which they sketched) that indicate awareness of the amortized complexity path.
- References called out leadership on a large infra migration and ownership of API-versioning across teams; the references used "led the migration" language — I can paste excerpt if helpful.

Given the totality, I'm still recommending L3. If Dev's concerns are about scale edges, let's capture those as specific 90-day expectations:
- Deliver a plan for multi-region replication with SLO tradeoffs
- Implement and benchmark hot-path optimization for one critical endpoint
- Pair with senior infra on incident postmortems during ramp

Offer guidance: recommend we extend final offer at $155k base + equity band A (4), sign-on $10k discretionary. Candidate has an external offer; we need to move by Thursday EOD to be competitive. Please advise if HR can approve offer authority to hiring manager or if Vivek needs to sign off.

Hannah
Engineering Manager, Core Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feedback discrepancy: Jordan Lee (Backend Engineer)

Team —

Thanks for the quick back-and-forth. Proposed next steps so we can move before Thursday: 

1) Calibration call: tomorrow 10:00am PT — invite sent: https://calendar.redwood.com/meeting/8f3b-quick-calibration. Please come prepared with 1-slide summary and the 90-day success criteria if you recommend L3.
2) Compensation decision: Vivek, can you confirm if we have flexibility to approve $155k + $10k sign-on and equity band A out of budget? If yes, we'll authorize Priya to draft an offer letter for Hannah to send upon HR memo.
3) Documentation: I'll attach the leveling rubric to the candidate file (leveling_rubric.pdf) and produce a short memo capturing the calibration.

Priya, please loop in TalentScout to confirm candidate timelines (I've cc'ed their email on a separate message). If the external offer deadline is sooner than Thursday we will escalate to an expedited approval process.

I'll follow up after the calibration with the memo and updated Greenhouse status.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior HR Business Partner
Redwood Inference
